checks.finding: Terms, actors, states, inputs and outputs are fixed concretely enough that two implementers would not build different behaviour. Field Definitions (requirements.md:908-961) fixes Resolver, Affected component, Matched Capability, capability_minimum_enforcement, Block and Resolver Evidence, each with a stated non-identity against the neighbouring sibling-epic concept. The CLI is fixed flag-by-flag (REQ-001, :232-238) with --feature required and never inferred. The write-mechanism fact is stated as one rule keyed on write-set size in four mutually consistent places: REQ-001 step (m) (:333-352, one-member set published directly, temp+fsync+rename, no journal), REQ-004 (:584-599, 'How Evidence reaches its live path depends on how many artifacts this invocation is publishing'), Roles and Permissions (:976-991, journaled transaction for a track output set vs. direct write when Evidence is the whole write set) and Security Boundaries (:1227-1233). The step-letter enumeration '(0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m)' used in REQ-001 and REQ-004 is incomplete -- Blocks raised at steps (b)/(d)/(e) (project-context-validation-failed, affected-component-resolution-failed, registry-validation-failed, contract-discovery-failed, canonicalizer-invocation-failed, dependency-subprocess-failed, dependency-output-malformed, and the ruling-C(1) mid-(e) recheck) are omitted -- but the governing predicate is not the step list: Security Boundaries :1227-1230 states the rule for 'A Block whose whole write set is Resolver Evidence' generally, which covers the omitted steps and leaves no mechanism choice open. Non-blocking clarification only; no FAIL basis under the Finding Evidence Gate.

The always-write-Evidence rule and the 'no live artifact' assertions for the snapshot-generation-mismatch Block directly conflict, and one of the two acceptance rows is impossible as written. (1) Exact conflicting text. requirements.md REQ-002 :399-404 -- 'Resolver Evidence (REQ-004) is still written on every Block, with two named exceptions: disabled-legacy-invocation ... and the self-referential output-schema-validation-failed case'; AC-012 (:858) repeats it; acceptance-tests.md TEST-012 (:61) binds it to fixtures -- 'every Block fixture in TEST-010 except disabled-legacy-invocation, and except the Evidence-itself-fails sub-case of output-schema-validation-failed ... writes a full Resolver Evidence record', and TEST-010 (:59) enumerates snapshot-generation-mismatch among its sixteen fixtures. REQ-001 step (m) (:333-352) and REQ-004 (:584-599) fix that this record reaches resolver-evidence.yaml's own LIVE path by a direct temp+fsync+rename, and Security Boundaries :1239-1245 confirms Evidence is 'fully written, at whichever step that Block is reached' on any Block except the two named. Against these: requirements.md AC-040 (:886) requires the snapshot-generation-mismatch fixture to Block 'and no artifact from this invocation reaches a live path', and acceptance-tests.md TEST-040 (:86) repeats 'no artifact reaches a live path'; requirements.md AC-057 (:903) and acceptance-tests.md TEST-057 (:103) require the registry-swapped-during-validation fixture to assert 'an empty capability_evaluations array ... and no live artifact'. resolver-evidence.yaml is an artifact of that invocation on a live path, so AC-040/TEST-040 contradict AC-012/TEST-012/REQ-002/REQ-004. AC-057/TEST-057 are additionally impossible on their own terms: capability_evaluations is a field of Resolver Evidence, so the row asserts the content of a file it simultaneously asserts was never written. Note the asymmetry with the sibling row authored under the same ruling pair: AC-058/TEST-058 assert the identical empty-capability_evaluations shape with NO 'no live artifact' clause, and AC-011 (:857) states the correct scoped form ('no facet-manifest.yaml, capability-summary.yaml, or project-context.resolved.json'), which identifies AC-040/AC-057 as unmaintained siblings rather than a considered position. (2) Downstream failure mode. A fixture author for the two snapshot-generation-mismatch fixtures and for registry-swapped-during-validation must assert either that resolver-evidence.yaml is absent (AC-040/AC-057/TEST-040/TEST-057) or that it is present carrying the Block record with an empty capability_evaluations array (AC-012/TEST-012/REQ-002/REQ-004/REQ-001 step (m)); one acceptance row fails by construction whichever behaviour is built, and the implementer cannot choose without amending a frozen Phase-1 document. This is the identical collision the package itself records at the AC-047/TEST-047 site, which ruling D(2) closed by stating the live-state obligation per target (acceptance-tests.md:93, 'every interrupted target other than resolver-evidence.yaml ... AND that resolver-evidence.yaml itself carries this invocation's own schema-valid Block record ... Asserting only the first half would contradict AC-012'); that per-target treatment was not propagated to the AC-040/AC-057 family. (3) Why this belongs to specification review. Both sides of the conflict live in Phase-1 artifacts only -- requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria table and acceptance-tests.md's test rows -- and no implementation, task-decomposition or quality-gate choice can satisfy both; only an amendment to these documents can close it, which is this gate's scope and not a later gate's. (4) Why Critical. AC-057/TEST-057 are an impossible acceptance criterion, and the fact at issue is the fail-closed durability of the Block record that REQ-004 exists to guarantee for downstream auditability -- a workflow-boundary guarantee, not a stylistic restatement. Remedy shape already exists in-package: scope the two clauses to the three publication artifacts, or state the obligation per target exactly as AC-047/TEST-047 now do.

Material negative, empty, boundary and failure paths implied by the requirements each carry an independently-triggerable acceptance row. Negative paths: one fixture per REQ-002 diagnostic-id row, sixteen enumerated by name plus a clean negative-control fixture (TEST-010, acceptance-tests.md:59); usage-error path separated from the Block path by exit code (AC-001/AC-013, TEST-001/TEST-013). Empty states: zero affected components with trigger_evaluations[] legitimately [] is fixtured separately from the general one-per-component rule (AC-018/TEST-018, requirements.md Edge Cases :1079-1098); empty conditional_facets: [] is fixed in Edge Cases :1133-1136; zero matched Capabilities is stated non-Blocking under either enforcement state (REQ-002 lite-check-source-undefined row, :382). Boundary/race states: pre-publication TOCTOU with a digest-identical but affected_components-different second fixture (AC-040/AC-048, TEST-040/TEST-048), the post-recheck race with journal rollback (AC-049/TEST-049), crash between two renames plus the unconvergeable-journal companion (AC-047/TEST-047), and the mid-pipeline step-(e) recheck (AC-057/TEST-057). Failure modes of dependencies: non-zero exit, zero-exit-malformed-stdout, and the absent-component inconsistency each have their own row (AC-058/TEST-058). WARN is covered on all three branch classes including the unmatched-Capability trigger (REQ-006 item d, TEST-027) with the diagnostics[] cardinality and the abort exception locked by TEST-056. The one acknowledged uncovered state, required-present-empty, is documented with its reason -- Epic A2's lite_policy schema is additionalProperties: false so no conformant Registry can express the key (TEST-009, acceptance-tests.md:58) -- which is an honest, cited exclusion rather than a silent gap.

Every assumption is either discharged by investigation or carries an explicit, owned pre-design/pre-task obligation. requirements.md Assumptions :1282-1305 lists three: sibling contracts landing unmodified from their Passed state (grounded in investigation.md INV-002/INV-004, with a stated follow-up-edit obligation if any changes materially); the protected-suffix reservation being live (INV-003, with an explicit re-verification step and a named alternative sequencing if it is not); and SKILL.md's unprotected status (INV-017, explicitly labelled a live-repository snapshot to be re-verified at implementation start, not a permanent guarantee). Open Questions :1309-1327: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are explicitly assigned out of scope to a future caller/epic and are mirrored in Non-goals :794-796, so neither is a decision this package must make; OQ-003 is recorded as resolved by INV-020 with a concrete file:line anchor plus a drift check (AC-053). Risks :1331-1423 name the Epic A2 required_lite_checks gap with an explicit owner ('owner: Epic A2's own maintainers, not this feature') and scope (Dependencies :140-163), and the aggregation-rule risk is stated as this feature's own new decision so that divergence surfaces as a spec-review finding rather than an implementation surprise. Nothing is left as an unresolved decision silently deferred past design/task decomposition.

Human/governance boundaries are in scope and each is stated testably. (a) Protected-path writes: Roles and Permissions :965-975 confines the future implementer to human-copy staging under specs/<feature>/human-copy/ for the three scripts' code only, never a direct agent write to the live protected path, and explicitly denies that human-copy is the mechanism by which generated artifacts acquire content; AC-026/TEST-026 requires the staged test.yml candidate with a correct MANIFEST.sha256 entry and marks its Status as resolving through a human cp action. (b) Scope boundary against plugins/**: Non-goals :805-810 plus AC-032/TEST-032 lock it by git diff of this package's own commits, and the Spec-Authoring-Time Manual Review Record (acceptance-tests.md:130-133) records the verification method. (c) Irreversible-change boundary: the unconvergeable-journal branch fails closed and hands off to a human operator rather than attempting repair (REQ-002 publication-journal-recovery row :372, Security Boundaries :1246-1254), and TEST-047 (acceptance-tests.md:93) makes that no-repair obligation assertable per target. (d) Frozen-contract authority: the feature is explicitly denied authority to revise Epic A1/A2/A3/A4 contracts (Non-goals :775-786), routing that decision back to the owning epic's own review. Each boundary is observable by a named fixture, diff check, or one-shot registration-time verification, so none is a boundary asserted but untestable.

Judged on this check's own predicate -- whether implementation-policy review would have to invent missing product behaviour -- the package is complete. The pipeline order is fixed step-by-step including the mandatory step-0 recovery scan and the staged-generation/publish-last ordering (REQ-001 :251-355); the refusal surface is a closed, sixteen-row machine-readable enum with per-row trigger conditions (REQ-002 :371-386); the new artifact's schema, cardinality, bidirectional-consistency and provenance-binding rules are fixed field-by-field along with its validator's own closed twelve-value check-id enum (REQ-004 :474-621); determinism is scoped to the track-exclusive output set with the one named enforcement-derived exception (REQ-003 :430-472, REQ-005); the caller-side contract names a concrete file:line insertion point with a position-sensitive drift check (REQ-007 :720-754, AC-053); and all 58 criteria map to test rows except the three documented Global rows (acceptance-tests.md:8-46). No product behaviour is absent that a design reviewer would have to supply. The one blocking defect this review found is not a missing-behaviour gap -- the behaviour is stated normatively in four places -- but a directly conflicting pair of acceptance rows, reported in full under CONTRADICTION; it must be closed before this package is handed on, and it is deliberately not double-counted here.
